To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Relational contracting, as an alternative to the traditional arm's length contracting, has been shown to be effective in reducing opportunism in transactions where the parties have repeated dealings.

the relational contracting literature is fragmented, with no single theory of relational contracting that can be applied to all projects, and that a new theory of relational contracting, based on the concept of displaced agency, is required to address the governance challenges posed by the discontinuity of participation in the project lifecycle.
the governance of large civil infrastructure projects is best viewed as an evolving series of discrete transactions in which key participants and stake holders rotate in and out.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and management of governance mechanisms to mitigate the hazards of relational contracting in complex, long lived projects.
the governance of complex, large scale, cross-sector, cross-cultural, multi-phase, multi-organizational, civil engineering infrastructure projects.
the governance of complex, large scale projects that are one off transactions for which there are no strong'shadow-of-the-future' effects to bind the participants together over time.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
relational contract theory is a useful tool for understanding project governance.
relational contracting is a form of governance that is based on trust, reciprocity and relational capital.
relational contracting is a form of governance that is supported by economic and sociological theories and by psychological and legal practices.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the relational contract theory is a theory which can be applied to the construction project management, but there are many factors that affect the relational contract theory.

the governance mechanisms that are most effective at managing the hazards of displaced agency are those that: (a) are most effective at mitigating the hazards of information asymmetry; (b) are most effective for mitigating the hazards associated with the 'bounded rationality' of the project participants; (c) provide the greatest flexibility in adapting to changing circumstances; and, (d) are most likely to be effective for managing the hazards associated with changing the project's governance structure over its lifetime.
the relational contract theory has been applied to a wide range of industries, but it has not been applied to the project industry.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the relational contract literature has not yet adequately addressed the challenges posed by 'displaced agency'.
the relational contracting literature has been dominated by economic and legal theory and that the sociological and psychological perspectives have been largely neglected.
a unified theory of relational contracting can be developed by integrating the insights of these diverse fields.
